# OCR fixtures

`MockOCRProvider` looks up a fixture by `sha256(image_bytes)[:16]`, so the same
bytes always produce the same extraction. That is what makes the end-to-end test
and the golden report files possible.

**No real documents are committed here, ever.** The fixture images are synthetic
byte strings generated by `tests/conftest.py`; the extractions beside them are
transcriptions of what the seven-model benchmark actually produced on the
thirteen-page corpus, retyped by hand with every identifier removed. That
includes the failure modes — the fixtures are not a picture of OCR working, they
are a picture of OCR working the way it measurably does.

## Files

| Fixture | What it exercises |
|---|---|
| `prescription_clean.json` | A legible prescription. Four medicines, all above the confidence floor. The happy path, and the interaction check has something to chew on. |
| `prescription_lowconf.json` | The digit failure. `900.2` where the paper says `100.2` — the misreading the benchmark actually produced — at a confidence below the floor, so it comes back `needs_verification` and renders with the raw text beside it. |
| `lab_report.json` | Lab values with the reference ranges printed on the same report. One below range, one above, and one with **no printed range at all**, which must come back `range_unavailable` and must not be flagged. |
| `discharge_summary.json` | Diagnoses and a procedure, which become `condition_*` and `surgery_*` facts on the document channel — the other half of a contradiction when the patient says something different. |
| `contains_aadhaar.json` | An Aadhaar number in the header, as the benchmark corpus contained. Proves the redaction pass masks it before it reaches a row. This is the fixture behind `tests/safety/test_redaction.py`. |

## Adding one

Generate the bytes deterministically, take the hash, and name the file after it:

```python
from app.adapters.ocr.mock import fixture_key
key = fixture_key(b"...")   # -> "1f4a2b..."
```

The extraction body is a `DocumentExtraction`, minus `document_id` (the provider
fills it in from the upload).
